Solicitation Document Description: .1	This RFP is an invitation by the City of Toronto (the “City”) to prospective Suppliers to submit Bids for Equity and Training Services as further described in Part 3 (Requirements for Deliverables):  The selected Supplier will be required to enter into an agreement with the City for the provision of the Deliverables. The final agreement shall be substantially in the form found in Part 2 (FORM OF AGREEMENT). The number of awarded Suppliers will depend on how many bids are successful after the evaluation. This RFP is divided into two (2) categories, with some categories further broken down into specific topics. Each topic within a category will be awarded separately to up to (3) successful suppliers. Suppliers may submit a Bid on any and all categories or specific topic depending on their expertise and capacity. Suppliers must clearly state which topic(s) they are applying to in their bid submission and how the requirements outlined in Section 3 are met in their bid for each of the topics they are submitting the bidding on. Suppliers may also submit separate bids for each of the topics should they wish to.  The term of the agreement for categories or topic services is to be for a period of one year with an option in favour of the City to extend the agreement on the same terms and conditions for an additional term of up to four (4) additional one (1) year terms under the terms and conditions of this Agreement. .4	Category Breakdown and Services:                     Category A – Design, Development and Delivery Services.  Category A will be awarded to up to three (3) Suppliers for each topic area, for a total of up to 36 Suppliers. Detailed descriptions of the following topic areas are found under Part 3 of this RFP:  1. Equity, Diversity and Inclusion 2. Accessibility and Disability Inclusion 3. Anti-racism (awards for each topic below will be made to up to three separate Suppliers) 	3.1. General 	3.2. Anti-Indigenous racism 	3.3. Anti-Black racism 	3.4. Antisemitism 	3.5. Islamophobia 	3.6. Anti-Asian racism 4. Human Rights / Workplace Discrimination and Harassment 5. Truth and Reconciliation 6. 2SLGBTQ+ Education 7. Gender Equity and Inclusion Each Supplier is permitted to bid on any category or topic based on their expertise and capability. When the Supplier submits their bids, they may consolidate the categories or topic areas into one proposal but must indicate which categories (i.e., Category A or B or both) or topic areas they are submitting for and showcase their qualifications and experience. If the supplier provides a list of course offerings, please state which topic area the course aligns with or falls under. Category B – Off-the-shelf Digital Course Category B services will be awarded to up to three (3) Suppliers. Detailed descriptions of the category B services are found under Part 3 of this RFP.

Solicitation Document Description: This RFSQ is an invitation by the City to qualify a minimum of three (3) and a maximum of ten (10) General Contractors for future eligibility for the purpose of establishing a Roster to carry out minor additions, rehabilitation and building repairs to various Parks, Forestry and Recreation facilities.   Description of Deliverables Successful Respondents making up the roster will undertake the construction and delivery of new or improvement work assignments of various scales and complexity, as work assignments arise, up to a maximum contract value per work assignment of $500,000.00, excluding taxes.   Successful Respondents making up the Roster shall be required to provide a response to a Request for Quotations (RFQ) per work assignment, per scope of work and contract documents provided in the work assignment RFQ. The lowest bidder, who meets the mandatory requirements will be awarded the work assignment.  Tasks and deliverables may vary per work assignment, but are generally within the scope of work described

Solicitation Document Description: optionsThe City of Toronto (“the City”) has made a commitment to combating climate change. In 2019, Toronto City Council declared a climate emergency, and in 2021, it updated the City’s TransformTO Climate Action Strategy to include the goal of reaching net zero GHG emissions by 2040, one of the most ambitious targets in North America.  •	The purpose of this project is to develop a long-term, comprehensive GHG Mitigation Strategy for TW, tailored to TW’s needs and circumstances, with a focus on the next 15 years (i.e., to 2040) but with consideration for the longer-term as well. The Strategy will meet the following high-level objectives: o	Address Council-mandated GHG reduction targets as specified in the City’s TransformTO Net Zero policy of net zero by 2040 (noting that the City’s corporate goals are not necessarily appropriate for TW, and the scope of this project includes setting appropriate goals for TW). o	Coordinate and prioritize TW’s GHG mitigation work. o	Identify financial opportunities and avoid financial risks.  o	Showcase TW’s climate mitigation leadership.  •	The scope of work includes all engineering services related to the development of the GHG Mitigation Strategy and all deliverables in this RFP.  •	Broadly the scope includes the following items: o	Define mission, vision, and guiding principles for TW GHG Mitigation Strategy.  o	Review background information, studies, regulations, and policies related to GHG mitigation. o	Develop the economic framework that will be used to support decision-making for GHG emission reductions.  o	Identify and evaluate potential GHG reduction technologies and strategies and perform a screening analysis for proposed GHG reduction projects.  o	Develop decision-support tools to help Toronto Water to consider GHG emissions in decision-making and tracking.  o	Establish GHG reduction targets aligned with the City’s TransformTO Net Zero policy using the identified projects that can be undertaken to achieve GHG reduction targets. o	Create communications materials to communicate various aspects of the TW GHG Mitigation Strategy to Toronto Water staff and other stakeholders. o	Summarize past and ongoing efforts relating to Scope 3 emissions and recommend a path forward for considering Scope 3. o	Prepare a final GHG Mitigation Strategy Report that integrates findings from all phases of the project, including recommendations for implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

Solicitation Document Description: •	  Toronto Water (TW) through this Request for Proposal (RFP) is soliciting proposals from qualified Suppliers to provide professional services to study and provide platform(s) recommendations with their pros and cons where TW can access or retrieve geo-spatial documents among other document/file formats such as text, data, audio, 3D images, pdf, etc. •	The selected Supplier will be expected to research, and make recommendations for the necessary services, software, and/or hardware that meet the needs of TW’s central platform for accessing geo-spatial and other documents in their respective repositories. •	In addition, the recommended platform(s) will be scalable, and seamlessly integrate or interface with existing or future document management systems within TW and the City of Toronto.  •	TW currently has several electronic document management systems (EDMSs) in silos that are neither integrated nor interfaced with one another. The objective of this project is to engage a Supplier, a company or consultant, to study and provide recommendations to TW to implement a centralized access or retrieval platform using any of the existing EDMS platforms or a net new platform as the case may be. The selected consultant will be required to conduct a thorough study and assessment of the current siloed TW and/or City of Toronto document management systems; the DMS of other jurisdictions (including outside Canada); and other DMSs available in the market. The study will identify the capabilities of the platform, or limitations that may impact their ability to serve as an effective centralized enterprise platform for TW. •	The recommended platform is expected to have the capabilities to access spatially enabled information and retrieve geospatial details. •	This Study is Phase 1, and a Phase 2 is planned as the Implementation Phase. •	The Supplier is advised that providing consulting services for Phase 1 is not a guarantee they will also be selected to provide their consulting services for Phase 2. Also, it is expected that any Phase 1 work and reporting by the Supplier will be free of bias that would favour them to provide Phase 2.

Due to the large volume of unanticipated/emergency work required, and in an effort to be able to service its clients in a reasonable and timely manner, the City reserves the right to enter into a Contract with two (2) successful General Contractors who have the highest evaluation scores (Part4 -Form B Technical Proposal and Qualifications) meeting mandatory requirements to perform the tasks associated with this Request for Proposal (RFP). Should the General Contractor have satellite locations available, this information must be provided by the General Contractor (Part 4 - Form C) for Award consideration. The work is spread out in two geographical areas, i.e. North & East Districts, and South (including Toronto Islands) & West Districts and one contractor will be hired for each geographical after evaluation by the City. Suppliers are required to indicate their preference of geographical area in their submission. The proponent with the highest score will be assigned their preferred geographical area while the second highest will be assigned the other geographical area. The City will make every effort to ensure an even distribution of work between the two successful Contractors. The Contractor must remain flexible to work at any geographical area. The City reserves the right to allocate any contract to one of the successful contractors, irrespective of the geographical area.  The term of the Contract is to be for a period of (3) three years from the date of award, with an option to extend the agreement on the same terms and conditions for an additional two, one (1) year terms. The option to renew is at the discretion of the City and will be subject to budget availability and General Contractor's performance.

Removal and disposal of existing hardscape elements, including unit paving, concrete paving, and rubberized surfacing.  2. Protection of existing trees during construction. 7.	Installation of new hardscape elements, including: o	Unit paving, cobblestone paving, and concrete paving o	Chipped granite fines surfaces o	Granite block wall to define cemetery border o	Rubberized surfacing for play area, and artificial turf for off-leash area o	Natural stone or concrete curbs o	Metal edging o	Armourstone barrier along the west side of the play area 8.	Planting bed preparation, sowing of meadow areas, sod installation, and planting of trees, shrubs, perennials, and plugs. 9.	Installation of temporary fencing around all newly planted areas. 10.	Supply and installation of new park furniture, including benches, picnic tables, café tables and chairs, seating blocks, bike rings, and park signage. 11.	Supply and installation of new play equipment. 12.	Installation of low fencing around planted areas and fencing around play area and off-leash area. 13.	Installation and hook up of new drinking fountain to water supply. 14.	Installation of subdrains and filtration trench for the off-leash area, and block stone wall. 15.	Installation of new irrigation system. 16.	Installation of new light poles, bollards, floodlight fixtures, linear LED fixtures, and candle lanterns. 17.	Installation of new electrical system. Note: Some items noted in this scope of work are optional items; inclusion in contract to be confirmed at time of contract award.

Solicitation Document Description: The Western Beaches Tunnel (WBT) system (refer to Figure 1) collects and treats combined sewer overflows (CSO) and stormwater from ten existing CSO and storm sewer outfalls. Constructed in the late 1990's, the system consists of a 3 metre diameter, 3.6 kilometre long storage tunnel that runs parallel to Lake Ontario, from approximately Parkside Drive to Strachan Avenue, with three main storage shafts (approximately 25 metres diameter by 35 to 40 metres deep) located at the Battery Park (785 Lake Shore Blvd. W.), Cowan (1075 Lake Shore Blvd. W.) and Glendale (1725 Lake Shore Blvd. W.) sites, six drop shafts, ten sewer interception chambers, nine lake isolation chambers, and a pumping station with ultra-violet (UV) disinfection system. The Parkside Drive sewer interception chamber (located about 130m west of the Glendale sewer interception chamber) includes an approximate 45m long open channel emergency overflow to the lake. The entire WBT system has an 85,000 cubic metre storage volume and was designed to improve water quality conditions at the City of Toronto’s nearby swimming beaches and along Toronto's waterfront.     This WBT Phase 2 construction project involves a complete retrofit of the existing Battery Park pumping station building. As an overview, the general work scope includes removal of all electrical, mechanical, HVAC, process, instrumentation, SCADA/automation, shaft access stairs, pumping system, tunnel flushing system, shaft sediment fluidization system and UV system equipment (the pumping station structure including the floors, walls and roof will be retained) and replacement with all new equipment. Related, but significantly less extensive, work is also required at the Cowan, Glendale and Parkside sites. A more detailed summary of the work scope consists of, but is not limited to, the following major work: 1.	Management of the construction works and integration with ongoing facilities and operations. 2.	Provision of all temporary measures and works (including equipment, piping, civil, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and control) to complete work under this Contract including disposal of any contaminated soil and groundwater, and management of any sewer infiltration/leakage flows. A major temporary measure will be the construction and operation of a temporary pumping system capable of pumping up to 300 L/s to remove inflow/infiltration and overflow water that enters the WBT system so that construction work can proceed under dry conditions within the system. 3.	Demolition, removal and modification of the existing equipment, piping, structures, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and control systems as shown on the drawings and described in the specifications. Disposal of removed unwanted equipment, piping, structures, excavated materials, dewatering water and contaminated materials off site resulting from the demolition, removal, excavation and construction works. Finish the removal and modification surfaces to match adjacent surface conditions by filling, grout, painting or other required means. 4.	Coordination and cooperation with the City is required for temporary measures and for continuous operation of the facilities, maintenance and access, connections to the existing facilities, installation of new equipment, buildings, structures, mechanical, electrical and control systems. Coordinate mechanical, process systems and electrical installations. 5.	Furnish, install and/or supervise installation, start-ups, testing, corrections if needed, commissioning and training. The project work scope includes:  (A)	Replacing the existing two pump system with 2 decant pumps and 2 dewatering pumps, including pump mounts and pump retrieval systems;  (B)	Install new actuators for the existing three flushing gates and the new lake water intake chamber isolation gate. Install a new trash rack and trash basket in the lake water pump chamber.; (C)	Installing new grit/sediment fluidization systems in the Battery Park shaft. There will be one fluidization system for the shaft that is gravity fed with lake water and one fluidization system for the pump sump that is pump fed with lake water. Installation of new stairs and a perimeter sediment/rock barrier wall around the pump sump.; (D)	Replace the existing UV system with a new up-to-date system including modifications to the UV forebay, grating and effluent weir; (E)	Installation of new composite samplers that have separate sample pumps and recirculation lines; (F)	Modifications to the existing Battery Park storage shaft roof hatches and provision of new hatches for equipment removal, access and cleaning; (G)	Replacement of the existing stairs in Battery Park shaft with new FRP stairs; (H)	Replacement of existing stairs at Glendale shaft with new FRP stairs: (I)	The installation of new stairs in the Cowan shaft with new FRP stairs; (J)	The supply of travel restraint systems on the upper ring channel inside the Battery Park shaft and training for use
Wards: Ward 4 Parkdale-High Park

Solicitation Document Description: RFP-22ECS-LU-02FP  The scope to be delivered under this RFP will consist of a number of storm drainage improvement Projects, which may include, but not be limited to: sanitary sewer upgrades, combined sewer upgrades, storm sewer upgrades, new storm or sanitary system infrastructure, trunk sewer upgrades, separation of CSO system through installation of new storm sewer systems, watercourse adjustment and restoration, in-line and off-line storage and box culverts, catch basin inlet controls, outfall/outlet control structures, stormwater management facilities (i.e. ponds, wetlands, tanks and tunnels) and other associated municipal infrastructure work and appurtenances. The approximate timeline for this Program is expected to be eight (8) years plus post construction services during the two year warranty period for each construction contract, for a total of ten (10) years.  The Basement Flooding Protection Program (BFPP) Assignments to be delivered under this RFP have been divided into two Bundles of work, and each Bundle will be awarded to one Consultant, for a total of two Consultants.  The scope of work in this RFP for Phase 5 of the Basement Flooding Protection Program (BF5) includes the main activities listed below:  • Program and project management services.  • EA studies review.  • Data collection.  • Hydraulic modelling.  • Preliminary design engineering services.  • Geotechnical/hydrogeological investigations.  • Detailed design engineering services.  • Excess soil management.  • Tender preparation and procurement support.  • Quality assurance materials testing during construction.  • Construction contract administration, including site inspection and field ambassadors.  • Post-construction services.  The BF5 Assignment Bundles included in the RFP, for which EA reports have already been completed, are as follows:  • Bundle 1: EA assignments moving forward for Area 40 (40-02, 40-03, 40-06, 40-07, 40-12, 40-13, and 40-14). The RFP will have a total capital delivery capacity of up to $115M, excluding HST, for Bundle 1 and its related add-on scope.  • Bundle 2: EA assignments moving forward for Areas 34, 36, 38, and 41 (34-06A/34-07A, 34-08, 34-12, 34-13, 36-12, 36-13, 38-24, and 41-01). Solicitation Document Description: •	The City of Toronto requires professional engineering services to analyze the trunk sewer systems servicing the Bermondsey and Massey Creek sewersheds to identify capacity constraints based on current and future growth scenarios, and to provide solution options, an assessment of those options and a preferred recommended solution.   •	The Golden Mile Secondary Plan Area (“the Golden Mile”) is located in Scarborough and is one of the many significant redevelopment areas within the City of Toronto, encompassing approximately 119 hectares along Eglinton Avenue East between Victoria Park Avenue and Birchmount Road. Current land use in the area consists of large-format retail buildings and surface parking with low-rise commercial and industrial buildings to the north and south of Eglinton Avenue East.   •	The Eglinton Crosstown Light Rail Transit (ECLRT) will pass through the Golden Mile and has five surface transit platforms constructed that will help transition the area into a mixed-use, transit-oriented community. A number of development applications have been submitted within the Golden Mile and are currently under review. The latest population proposed for the Golden Mile includes is approximately 67,000 new residents and 9,000 new jobs, which exceeds the City’s population forecasts.   •	Current sanitary drainage areas show that the Golden Mile is currently serviced by two trunk sewers: the Bermondsey Sanitary Trunk Sewer to the west and the Massey Creek Sanitary and Relief Trunk Sewers to the east, with a drainage divide generally at Warden Avenue. •	A master servicing report for the redevelopment of the Golden Mile was carried out by a landowners’ group in early 2020 and updated in 2022. Several servicing alternatives were considered and ultimately recommended upgrades on both the developer and City side to accommodate the Golden Mile development area. These previous studies and recommendations have led the City to this current study which will evaluate and confirm capacity in the trunk system considering the City projected 2051 populations and the latest proposed developments within a wider study area.   •	The Supplier will develop an implementation plan and strategy to prioritize and sequence the recommended wastewater system upgrades and improvements to align with projected incremental growth. The City anticipates the solution will benefit both the existing system and future growth.
Wards: Ward 16 Don Valley East

Solicitation Document Description: Background  Willowdale Park, located at 75 Hollywood Ave, North York, ON M2N 5S9, is being improved in line with the design developed in collaboration with the local Councillor, residents, other stakeholders.    The purpose of this Request for Tender (RFT) is to provide full general contracting construction supply and installation services for the Landscape Redevelopment Project, Willowdale Park Improvements, as required by the City of Toronto, Parks & Recreation, Capital Projects Division. It is expected that the winning bidder will comply with the standards, guidelines, policies and procedures of the relevant authorities and divisions, as well as with all applicable codes, by-laws, and regulations.   The park is home to the North York Tennis Club. Along with tennis facilities the park currently features a playground, splash pad, pathways, parking lot, open lawn areas and mature trees. There are plans to upgrade the park with a new playground and outdoor exercise station, as well as a new shade structure, seating, community message board, and bottle filling station. Existing concrete pathways will be redone with new concrete. The tennis courts will receive new fencing, lighting and repairs to the existing retaining wall. Excavation will be required to accommodate the construction of these features and upgrades.  Summary of work   Services expected to be completed include, but are not limited to, grading, drainage, site servicing, demolition & removals, clearing and grubbing, site/tree protection fencing, concrete flat work and concrete curbs/walls/pavements, walkways, armour stone walls, concrete ramp, concrete stairs, asphalt/unit paving, splash pad, fencing, tree and shrub planting, sodding, seating, playground, outdoor fitness, lighting, and shade structure. As most of the work is landscape architectural in nature and involves the extensive renovation of existing landscape elements, the contractor team shall be led by a landscape contractor experienced in leading and coordinating landscape renovation projects, with experience in playground installation.
Wards: Ward 18 Willowdale
